criteria: States each paper's title, timing, marks and section structure accurately
Distinguishes command words (describe/explain/assess/evaluate/suggest) and what each demands
Explains what AO1-AO4 each reward, including the fieldwork minimums within AO3 and AO4
Applies this understanding to judge whether a sample answer meets a given AO
S01_Scheme_of_Assessment_and_AOs.pass_threshold: Learner can state each paper's title, length, marks and weighting from memory, and correctly sort a set of sample question stems into the AO they mainly reward.

source.document: AQA GCSE Geography (8035) specification, sections 2 and 4

criteria: Defines a natural hazard accurately, including the idea of potential harm to people or property
Classifies hazard types (geological, meteorological/atmospheric) correctly
Explains at least two factors affecting hazard risk between places
Explains the process at each of the three plate margin types using correct tectonic vocabulary
S02_Natural_Hazards_and_Tectonic_Process.pass_threshold: Foundation: correctly defines a natural hazard, classifies at least three hazard types, and names the three plate margin types with one correct process each. Higher: explains why risk varies between places and links margin type to landform and hazard produced.

criteria: Correctly distinguishes primary from secondary effects and immediate from long-term responses
Uses accurate named figures (dates, magnitude, death toll) for both Chile 2010 and Nepal 2015
Explains, with reasoning, how wealth and development change the scale of effects and speed of response
Explains monitoring, prediction, protection and planning as distinct but related ways to reduce risk
S03_Tectonic_Hazards_Effects_Responses_a.pass_threshold: Foundation: correctly sorts effects and responses into the right categories and names one figure from each case study. Higher: compares Chile and Nepal explaining why wealth changed the effects and responses, and explains monitoring, prediction, protection and planning together.

criteria: Explains the three-cell model in enough detail to account for the pressure belts and trade winds
States accurate formation conditions and the global distribution of tropical storms
Labels and explains the eye, eye wall and rain bands correctly
Distinguishes primary from secondary effects and immediate from long-term responses, and links climate change to storm intensity
S04_Tropical_Storms.pass_threshold: Foundation: names the global distribution and formation conditions of tropical storms and labels the main structural features. Higher: explains the three-cell model and links storm distribution and possible future change to atmospheric circulation and climate change.

criteria: Gives accurate named figures for Typhoon Haiyan's effects
Names UK weather hazard types and explains the causes of Storm Desmond
Describes social, economic and environmental impacts of Storm Desmond and the response to it
Evaluates evidence for increasingly extreme UK weather with balanced reasoning
S05_Tropical_Storms_Case_Study_and_UK_We.pass_threshold: Foundation: gives named figures for Typhoon Haiyan and Storm Desmond and lists UK weather hazard types. Higher: explains how monitoring, prediction, protection and planning reduced (or could have reduced) impacts, and evaluates evidence that UK weather is becoming more extreme.

criteria: Explains at least two forms of evidence for climate change accurately
Correctly distinguishes natural from human causes of climate change
Describes effects on people and the environment with specific detail
Distinguishes mitigation from adaptation and evaluates the need for both
S06_Climate_Change.pass_threshold: Foundation: names evidence and at least one natural and one human cause of climate change, and gives one mitigation and one adaptation example. Higher: explains how each piece of evidence works and evaluates mitigation versus adaptation as different approaches.

criteria: Explains food chains, food webs, nutrient cycling and the impact of removing a component
Describes the global distribution of large-scale ecosystems in relation to latitude and climate
Describes rainforest climate and correctly labels its four vegetation layers
Explains plant and animal adaptations and why interdependence makes the rainforest a fragile system
S07_Ecosystems_and_Rainforest_Characteri.pass_threshold: Foundation: describes a food chain/web and names the four rainforest layers with basic adaptations. Higher: explains what happens to the whole ecosystem if one component changes, and explains interdependence in the rainforest as a system.

criteria: Explains that deforestation rates have varied rather than only ever risen or fallen
Names and explains at least three causes and three impacts of Amazon deforestation with specific detail
Explains the value of tropical rainforests to both people and the environment
Evaluates at least two management strategies and reaches a supported judgement
S08_Rainforest_Deforestation_and_Managem.pass_threshold: Foundation: names at least three causes and three impacts of Amazon deforestation and one management strategy. Higher: explains the trend in deforestation rates over time and evaluates whether management strategies can genuinely balance development with conservation.

criteria: Describes cold environment climate and defines permafrost and the active layer accurately
Explains interdependence between climate, permafrost, soils, plants, animals and people
Names specific Alaska development opportunities and challenges with detail
Evaluates at least one strategy for balancing development with conservation
S09_Cold_Environments.pass_threshold: Foundation: describes cold environment climate and names development opportunities and challenges for Alaska. Higher: explains how climate, permafrost, soils, plants, animals and people are interdependent, and evaluates how development and conservation can be balanced.

criteria: Distinguishes constructive from destructive waves using swash and backwash correctly
Names and explains all four processes of coastal erosion accurately
Distinguishes weathering from mass movement and names at least one example of each type
Explains how rock structure and type produce concordant and discordant coastlines
S10_UK_Landscapes_and_Coastal_Processes.pass_threshold: Foundation: locates upland and lowland UK areas and names the four coastal erosion processes with a basic definition. Higher: explains why waves, weathering and mass movement type vary with rock structure and exposure.

criteria: Explains the formation of headlands and bays with reference to rock resistance
Explains the full cave-arch-stack-stump erosional sequence correctly and in order
Explains beach, sand dune and spit/bar formation with correct process vocabulary
Uses specific, accurately located Purbeck examples to support the explanation
S11_Coastal_Landforms.pass_threshold: Foundation: describes the formation sequence of at least three landforms and locates them on the Purbeck coast. Higher: explains the full formation sequence from headland to cave-arch-stack-stump, and from sand dune to established dune system.

criteria: Explains at least one hard and one soft engineering option with accurate costs and benefits
Defines managed retreat and explains its costs and benefits
Explains the reasons for the specific strategy used at Cleveleys, using located detail
Evaluates and compares strategies, reaching a supported judgement
S12_Coastal_Management.pass_threshold: Foundation: names hard and soft engineering options with one cost and one benefit each. Higher: evaluates which approach best suits Cleveleys, and compares it with a managed retreat scheme.

criteria: Explains freeze-thaw weathering and both glacial erosion processes (abrasion and plucking) accurately
Explains the formation of at least three erosional landforms with correct process detail
Distinguishes till from outwash and explains at least two depositional landforms
Sequences landform formation correctly rather than describing landforms in isolation
S13_Glacial_Processes_and_Erosional_Land.pass_threshold: Foundation: names the main erosional and depositional landforms with a basic description. Higher: explains the process (freeze-thaw, abrasion, plucking, rotational slip) responsible for each landform in sequence.

criteria: Names and correctly locates specific Lake District glacial landforms
Explains at least two economic activities and one land-use conflict with reasoning
Explains social, economic and environmental impacts of tourism with specific detail
Evaluates management strategies and reaches a supported judgement
S14_Lake_District_Landforms_and_Tourism.pass_threshold: Foundation: names at least two Lake District landforms and two economic activities with a tourism impact. Higher: explains land-use conflicts between activities and evaluates whether management strategies successfully balance them.

criteria: Explains urbanisation and correctly contrasts the rate and pattern between HICs and LICs/NEEs
Explains rural-urban migration using push-pull theory, and defines natural increase correctly
Locates Lagos accurately and explains its importance
Explains specific social and economic opportunities urban growth has brought to Lagos
S15_Urbanisation_and_Lagos_Growth.pass_threshold: Foundation: explains urbanisation and names Lagos's causes of growth. Higher: explains why urbanisation rates differ between HICs and LICs/NEEs and links Lagos's growth to both migration and natural increase.

criteria: Explains why squatter settlements such as Makoko developed, with specific detail
Explains at least two service-provision challenges (water/sanitation/energy, health/education) with detail
Links unemployment, the informal economy and crime with clear reasoning
Evaluates a named scheme improving quality of life for the urban poor, reaching a judgement
S16_Lagos_Challenges_and_Solutions.pass_threshold: Foundation: names at least three Lagos challenges with a specific detail each. Higher: explains why rapid, unplanned growth causes these challenges and evaluates a named scheme improving quality of life for the urban poor.

criteria: Describes UK population distribution and locates Manchester accurately
Explains the impact of national and international migration on Manchester with specific detail
Explains social, economic and environmental opportunities with named examples
Explains social, economic and environmental challenges, linking them to Manchester's economic history
S17_UK_Cities_and_Manchester.pass_threshold: Foundation: locates Manchester and names two opportunities and two challenges. Higher: explains how migration has shaped Manchester's growth and character, and how opportunities and challenges are linked to its economic history.

criteria: Defines urban sprawl and the rural-urban fringe correctly
Explains the reasons for, and features of, the Salford Quays and MediaCityUK regeneration with specific detail
Explains at least three features of sustainable urban living
Explains and evaluates transport strategies for reducing congestion
S18_Urban_Sprawl_Regeneration_and_Sustai.pass_threshold: Foundation: defines urban sprawl and names the reasons for, and features of, the Salford Quays regeneration. Higher: evaluates whether regeneration and sustainability strategies fully resolve the problems of sprawl and congestion.

criteria: Classifies HIC/LIC/NEE correctly and explains what distinguishes them
Names and explains economic and social development measures accurately
Explains DTM stages correctly, linking birth/death rate change to development
Explains causes and consequences of uneven development, and evaluates at least two strategies to reduce it
S19_Development_and_the_Development_Gap.pass_threshold: Foundation: names development measures and DTM stages, and lists strategies to reduce the gap. Higher: evaluates limitations of development measures and explains multiple causes and consequences of uneven development.

criteria: Explains tourism's costs and benefits for Jamaica's development with specific detail
Locates Nigeria accurately and explains its regional and international importance
Explains Nigeria's industrial structure, TNCs and trading relationships with named detail
Evaluates environmental impacts and quality-of-life effects, reaching a supported judgement
S20_Nigeria_Case_Study.pass_threshold: Foundation: locates Nigeria and names its industry, trading partners and aid. Higher: evaluates whether TNCs and international aid have made Nigeria's quality of life better or worse overall.

criteria: Explains at least two causes of UK deindustrialisation with named detail
Explains the shift to a post-industrial economy with named examples
Explains rural growth and decline with specific located examples
Explains infrastructure investment and evaluates strategies addressing the north-south divide
S21_UK_Economic_Change.pass_threshold: Foundation: names causes of UK deindustrialisation and one example each of rural growth, rural decline and infrastructure investment. Higher: evaluates whether regional strategies are closing the north-south divide.

criteria: Explains why food, water and energy matter to wellbeing and development
Explains global inequality in resource supply and consumption using scarcity concepts
Explains UK water demand trends and quality management measures with detail
Explains the UK's supply-demand mismatch and names a specific transfer scheme correctly
S22_Resource_Management_and_UK_Water.pass_threshold: Foundation: explains why resources matter and describes the UK's water supply-demand pattern. Higher: explains why water must be transferred within the UK and evaluates the trade-offs involved.

criteria: Explains global patterns of water surplus and deficit with correct reasoning
Explains factors affecting availability and impacts of water insecurity with specific detail
Explains the Lesotho Highlands scheme's advantages and disadvantages accurately
Explains the Kenyan sand dam scheme and evaluates it against the large-scale scheme
S23_Global_Water_Resource_Option.pass_threshold: Foundation: names factors affecting water availability and one large-scale and one small-scale water scheme. Higher: evaluates the Lesotho Highlands scheme's costs and benefits against Kenyan sand dams as contrasting approaches.

criteria: Explains the synoptic, multi-scale nature of issue evaluation
Explains the purpose and use of the pre-release resources booklet
Identifies stakeholders and weighs advantages, disadvantages and alternatives
Reaches a decision clearly justified with specific evidence and explained interrelationships
S24_Issue_Evaluation_Skills.pass_threshold: Foundation: describes the pre-release booklet's role and the typical question sequence. Higher: produces a justified decision that weighs stakeholders, advantages, disadvantages and alternatives using evidence from the booklet.

criteria: States the fieldwork requirement and explains how fieldwork is assessed
Writes a testable, theory-linked enquiry question or hypothesis
Distinguishes primary from secondary evidence and justifies location choice
Identifies fieldwork risks and explains specific, realistic ways to reduce them
S25_Fieldwork_Enquiry_Questions_and_Data.pass_threshold: Foundation: states the fieldwork requirement and names the theory behind an enquiry question. Higher: writes a testable enquiry question, links it to geographical theory, and justifies data sources, locations and risk-reduction measures.

criteria: Distinguishes primary/secondary and physical/human data with specific examples
Explains all three sampling methods correctly with a suitable example for each
Justifies data collection method choices for a specific enquiry
Selects, accurately describes and justifies an appropriate presentation method
S26_Fieldwork_Data_Types_and_Sampling.pass_threshold: Foundation: names sampling methods and presentation techniques with a basic description. Higher: justifies the choice of data collection and presentation methods for the Cleveleys and Salford Quays enquiries.

criteria: Describes, analyses and explains results, going beyond description to reasoned explanation
Uses an appropriate statistical technique correctly to support analysis
Identifies and offers a plausible explanation for an anomaly
Reaches a conclusion directly answering the enquiry question, using specific evidence
S27_Fieldwork_Analysis_and_Conclusions.pass_threshold: Foundation: describes a data pattern and states one problem with a data collection method. Higher: analyses linked data sets using statistics, explains an anomaly, and reaches a conclusion that answers the original enquiry question.

criteria: Suggests specific, relevant further data to strengthen an enquiry
Judges reliability using sample size, data problems and limitations correctly
Outlines the Cleveleys enquiry's question, methods, analysis and conclusion accurately
Outlines the Salford Quays enquiry's question, methods, analysis and conclusion accurately
S28_Fieldwork_Evaluation_and_School_Enqu.pass_threshold: Foundation: states one improvement and one reliability judgement for an enquiry, and outlines both enquiries. Higher: evaluates how reliable the conclusions from Cleveleys and Salford Quays are, and what further data would improve each.

criteria: Reads and states latitude/longitude coordinates correctly
Describes a distribution using direction, named places and comparative language
Gives four- and six-figure grid references correctly (eastings before northings)
Measures straight and curved-line distance accurately using the map scale
S29_Atlas_Maps_and_OS_Map_Basics.pass_threshold: Foundation: gives a four-figure grid reference and reads a map scale correctly. Higher: gives a six-figure grid reference, measures a curved route accurately, and explains an association shown on a thematic map.

criteria: Reads gradient, contours and spot heights correctly and links contour spacing to steepness
Identifies named landscape features from contour patterns with accurate description
Constructs a cross-section correctly using the paper-strip method
Draws a well-evidenced inference supported by specific grid references or map evidence
S30_OS_Maps_Relief_and_Landscape_Feature.pass_threshold: Foundation: reads a spot height and describes one landscape feature shown on a map. Higher: constructs and interprets a cross-section and draws a well-evidenced inference about physical or human landscape from map evidence.

criteria: Infers human activity, including tourism, correctly from map symbol evidence
Compares two maps or sources accurately, identifying specific change with grid references
Draws a clear, roughly-to-scale sketch map or field sketch with title, key/labels and north arrow where relevant
Distinguishes ground, aerial and satellite images, and writes explanatory annotations rather than bare labels
S31_Maps_with_Photographs_and_Annotation.pass_threshold: Foundation: labels one feature on a photograph and describes what a symbol suggests about human activity. Higher: draws a clearly labelled field sketch from a photograph and compares it accurately against a map of the same area.

criteria: Selects an appropriate graph or chart type and justifies the choice against the data type
Constructs or completes a graph/chart/thematic map accurately with correct labels, scale and key
Interprets isoline gradient and estimates intermediate values correctly
Interprets a complex representation (population pyramid, choropleth map) with specific, accurate description
S32_Graphical_Skills.pass_threshold: Foundation: names an appropriate graph type for a given data set and plots simple data accurately. Higher: justifies the choice of graphical technique and interprets a complex data representation such as a population pyramid or choropleth map correctly.

criteria: Calculates mean, median, mode, range and interquartile range correctly from given data
Calculates percentage change correctly and interprets its direction
Describes a bivariate relationship and distinguishes interpolation from extrapolation correctly
Identifies and explains a specific weakness in selective statistical presentation
S33_Numerical_and_Statistical_Skills.pass_threshold: Foundation: calculates a mean and a simple percentage change correctly. Higher: calculates interquartile range, describes a scatter graph relationship with interpolation/extrapolation, and spots weaknesses in selective statistical presentation.

criteria: Distinguishes qualitative/quantitative and primary/secondary data with specific, correct examples
Identifies GIS, satellite imagery or another digital source and explains a specific relevant use
Writes with a clear escalation from description to analysis and, where required, critical evaluation
Reaches a well-evidenced conclusion that explicitly weighs evidence and answers the question asked
Uses accurate spelling, punctuation, grammar and correct specialist terminology throughout
S34_Data_Sources_Enquiry_Writing_and_SPa.pass_threshold: Foundation: distinguishes primary from secondary and qualitative from quantitative data, and writes a clear descriptive paragraph. Higher: plans a full enquiry sequence, writes a well-structured extended argument reaching an evidenced conclusion, and uses accurate spelling, punctuation and specialist terminology throughout.

criteria: Answers accurately across all three papers without needing prompting on which topic applies
Uses named case studies, locations and the Cleveleys/Salford Quays enquiries correctly and specifically
Applies cartographic, graphical, numerical and statistical skills correctly to unfamiliar map, graph and data resources
Reaches and justifies a reasoned decision on the issue-evaluation question, weighing evidence from the resource booklet
Uses accurate spelling, punctuation, grammar and specialist terminology on SPaG-assessed extended questions
exam_rubric.pass_threshold: Performance consistent with the grade the learner is aiming for, judged against the levels of response bands in `rubric.json`'s `exam_rubric`. AQA sets exact grade boundaries per series rather than a fixed mark table; there is no foundation/higher tier split in AQA GCSE Geography 8035 (all candidates sit the same papers).

source.document: AQA GCSE Geography (8035) specification, Scheme of Assessment (Papers 1, 2 and 3)
source.reference: AQA 8035 specification, section 2.2 Scheme of assessment
